column1: # Leak-scan allowlist — every row is one exception, with its class, its credential,
#   rule <TAB> path-glob <TAB> sha256:<12> <TAB> class <TAB> credential <TAB> reason <TAB> expires
# Rules: a row matches one rule, one path glob, and one VALUE digest. A different
# value at the same path is still a finding. A `*` path glob is allowed because the
# digest still pins the one value, so there is no path-wide row.
# class: `constant` for a value that is permanent (a published password, a public
# key, a reserved-domain address, a test fixture) — expiry does not apply, so it
# reads `never` (a date is accepted and never expires); or `debt` for an allowance
# a card will clear — it carries that card's date (YYYY-MM-DD). A debt row past its
# date is a finding; a constant row never expires. A debt carrying `never` is a
# credential: `yes` when the value is a secret a person could present to a live
# system, `no` otherwise. Every scan prints the count next to the row count, so a
# reviewer sees how many secrets the allowlist waives.
# A row's reason must not contain the row's own value: that row matches itself,
# and "every row matched at least once" would prove nothing. Delete the row when
# the value is gone; do not change its class or date without a reason here.
